scenes.title: Learn before pitching
scenes.visual: Founder reviews an anonymous learning question.
scenes.narration: A customer conversation helps you learn about a person’s experience. Prepare a guide around one question from your validation plan. Do not lead with your product or try to collect agreement. Preparing this guide does not recruit anyone or conduct an interview.

scenes.title: Open with permission
scenes.visual: Adult participant can freely decline a fictional conversation.
scenes.narration: Explain the purpose and expected time, make participation voluntary, and say they can decline a question or stop. Ask appropriate permission before any recording. Use anonymous notes where possible and do not promise confidentiality you cannot deliver.

scenes.title: Ask about a recent experience
scenes.narration: Ask about the last time the person tried the relevant task. What happened, what did they try and what happened next? Recent accounts are more useful than asking whether everyone likes your idea. Keep the group and context specific.

scenes.title: Probe without suggesting answers
scenes.narration: Ask what they mean, what mattered, and whether they can describe a specific example. Do not suggest that they were frustrated or that your app would help. Accept that the current approach may work well. Avoid arguing with an answer that weakens your assumption.

scenes.title: Keep accounts and interpretations separate
scenes.visual: Editable anonymous reported-account and inference columns.
scenes.narration: A conversation gives someone’s reported account, not independent proof of every event or future behaviour. Record source code and context, distinguish notes from exact quotes, and label your interpretation. Do not invent quotes, frequency, payment intent or representative conclusions.

scenes.title: Build the guide
scenes.narration: Create your Neutral Conversation Guide with the learning question, opening, context prompt, core questions, probes, rewrites, notes and close. Keep access pending until arranged. The next lesson plans ethical recruitment of relevant participants.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Ask to understand, not to win agreement.

children: A
neutral question
does not suggest the answer. A
recent-experience prompt
asks about a specific event. A
probe
clarifies an account without putting words in someone’s mouth.
Leading
“Wouldn’t our app make registration easier?”
Neutral
“Tell me about the last time you found registration. What did you try?”
Assumed feeling
“How frustrated were you?” assumes frustration.
Open probe
“What mattered to you in that situation?” permits a different answer.
Use one learning question from your test plan.
Explain purpose/time, voluntary participation and stop/decline.
Ask about a recent relevant experience.
Explore actions, workarounds, outcomes and what mattered.
Use neutral probes; accept that current approaches may work.
Close respectfully and separate reported accounts from interpretations.

Permission for a conversation is not permission to record. Avoid unnecessary personal details or sensitive topics. Exact quotes must be actually captured and permitted; otherwise label paraphrases as notes. Do not invent accounts or treat one person as representative.
Future preference, compliments and a clear explanation do not prove adoption or payment. Keep those claims separate. This worksheet prepares questions only; it sends no messages and recruits nobody.
Review validation test plan
